cve_summary: The tipc_nl_publ_dump function in net/tipc/socket.c in the Linux kernel through 4.6 does not verify socket existence, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a dumpit operation.
commit_message:
tipc: check nl sock before parsing nested attributes

Make sure the socket for which the user is listing publication exists
before parsing the socket netlink attributes.

Prior to this patch a call without any socket caused a NULL pointer
dereference in tipc_nl_publ_dump().

Tested-and-reported-by: Baozeng Ding <sploving1@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Richard Alpe <richard.alpe@ericsson.com>
Acked-by: Jon Maloy <jon.maloy@ericsson.cm>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Handles the dumping of TIPC (Transparent Inter-Process Communication) socket information via netlink.

Parameters: 
skb (struct sk_buff *): Pointer to the socket buffer containing the netlink message.
cb (struct netlink_callback *): Pointer to the netlink callback structure containing context for the operation.

Returns: 
int: The length of the socket buffer on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function first checks if a socket port ID is provided; if not, it parses the netlink message to retrieve it. If the operation is already completed (indicated by the 'done' flag), it returns immediately. It then looks up the TIPC socket associated with the port ID and locks the socket. The function proceeds to list the published information of the socket, updating the 'last_publ' and 'done' flags as necessary. Finally, it updates the callback arguments with the current state and returns the length of the socket buffer.
"""
